cover.title: My Story
cover.subtitle: Everything, that happened, happened not to you, but for you.

content: Every story has a beginning, and mine starts in a small room with a big window. The light came in every morning like it had somewhere important to be, and so did I, even before I knew where.
[photo_1]

My mother says I asked questions before I could properly walk. Why is the sky doing that. Where does the water go. What is inside a radio. Nobody had all the answers, and somehow that felt like a promise rather than a problem.
[quote_1]

By the time I was ten, I had taken apart three clocks and successfully reassembled none of them. But I had learned the most important lesson of my life: things are made of smaller things, and smaller things can be understood.

photo_1.caption: The room with the big window.

quotes.quote_1: Curiosity was never a phase for me. It was the whole personality.

content: These were the years I stopped taking things apart and started putting things together. Two photos from this time survive, and they tell the whole story better than I can.
[photo_2]
The first is from the day I built something that actually worked. It was ugly. It was held together with tape and hope. But it worked, and I have been chasing that exact feeling ever since.
[photo_3]
The second is from a little later, when I realized that building alone was only half of it. The other half was building for someone. That changed everything about how I saw the work.

photo_2.caption: The first thing that actually worked.

photo_3.caption: Building for someone, not just something.

content: Not every chapter has pictures. Some are just thinking, and reading, and long walks where the only thing that happened was that an idea slowly turned from wrong into right.
This was a decade of listening more than talking. I learned that the loudest idea in the room is rarely the best one, and that patience is a skill you can actually practice.
[quote_1]
When I look back, this quiet stretch is the part I am most grateful for. Nothing dramatic happened, and that was exactly the point.

quotes.quote_1: The best ideas arrive quietly, and only if you leave the door open.

content: And then the pace picked up. Three photos for this chapter, because one could never hold it.
[photo_4]
The first is the leap. The moment I decided to stop preparing for the work and simply do the work.
[photo_1]
The second is the people. None of the good things happened alone, and I have the receipts to prove it.
[photo_2]
The third is now. Which is to say, unfinished, on purpose. The best part of any story is the page you have not written yet.
